# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (cand_0002; explainability; REQUIRED)

Edit space: ONLY the system prompt (`prompt.md`). tools.py is NOT in the editable set, so
every fix is a system-prompt edit grounded in THIS iteration's `./trajectories/`.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by leverage = # trials affected × score recoverable)
| rank | cluster | tasks (trials) | shared root cause | tag | change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Wasted round on wrong reply format** | 32468(5/5), 52216(5/5), 55457(5/5), 347-49(3/5), 40467(3/5), 374-9(2/5) — **23 of 50 trials** | On round 1 the agent replies with hallucinated tool-call XML (`<function_calls>`, `<invoke name="execute_python">`, `<invoke name="computer">`, `<parameter name="code">`) instead of a ```python fence. NOTHING executes → an error round is burned. With only ~5 rounds, complex tasks then run out of inspect+fix cycles. EVERY currently-passing task wastes 0 rounds; the failing/flaky tasks concentrate the waste. | KNOWLEDGE / output-contract | Add an explicit OUTPUT CONTRACT at the very top of the prompt. |
| 2 | **Literal output format not matched exactly** | 40467 (t0) | Instruction shows the exact target text `From 01-Jan to 05-Jan`; t0 wrote `TEXT(...,"d-mmm")` → renders `1-Jan` not `01-Jan` → 0.0. The 4 passing trials used `dd-mmm`. Seed scored 1.00; cand_0001 regressed it to 0.80 via this format slip. | KNOWLEDGE (format precision) | Add a rule: reproduce a shown literal result format character-for-character; pick the format code that yields it (`01`→`dd`/`00`). |
| — | Deep per-task logic (skipped) | 32468 (rolling-12-mo SUMIFS), 52216 (which cell drives the INDEX-MATCH region lookup), 347-49 (delete-blank-rows-above-marker exact block), 55457 (instruction is a lone nbsp — intent unknowable), 374-9 (output-row mapping fails on hidden files 2&3) | Not a shared, prompt-addressable class — the correct answer differs per task and the source files for hidden test cases 2&3 are unavailable, so any general rule risks overfitting/regression. | (skipped) | No safe general edit; the round-1 fix (rank 1) gives these tasks more usable rounds. |

## Changes made (one row per edit)
| cluster | edit class | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Add missing output-contract (menu: output contract) | prompt.md — new "OUTPUT CONTRACT" block at top | States: reply with EXACTLY ONE ```python fence, never XML/tool-call syntax; only fenced code runs; a non-fenced reply wastes a round. General to every task and every round. | YES — see verify below. |
| 2 | Add missing rule (menu: missing-rule / worked counterexample) | prompt.md — new sub-bullet under step 4 | Reproduce a shown literal format character-for-character; choose the format code that yields it (`01`→`dd`, `05`→`00`, `Jan`→`mmm`); a `1-Jan` where `01-Jan` was shown is graded wrong. | YES — see verify below. |

## Verify-the-fix + blast-radius (one line per edit)
- **Edit 1 (output contract).** REAL: 23/50 trials this iteration emit tool-call XML on round 1 and get the harness error "No python code block was found ... the round was wasted" (verified by scanning all `rollouts/val/*__cand_0001__t*.json`). The exact hallucinated tokens were extracted: `function_calls`, `invoke name="execute_python"`, `invoke name="computer"`, `parameter name="code"` — the rule names them explicitly. SAFE (bounded, behavioral): the 4 passing tasks 47484/418-29/53161/160-6 waste **0/5** rounds each — they already reply with a fence, so an explicit fence rule cannot change what they DO or compute; it only removes the wasted round on the fumbling trials. VERIFIED: rule is present, general, unambiguous, and matches the harness's actual contract (the user turn already demands "exactly ONE python code block").
- **Edit 2 (format precision).** REAL: 40467 t0 (reward 0.0) wrote `d-mmm`→`1-Jan` while the instruction shows `01-Jan`; the 4 passing trials wrote `dd-mmm`. SAFE (bounded trigger): fires only when the instruction contains an explicit literal-format sample; and "match the shown format exactly" is the graded-correct behavior, so it cannot turn a currently-correct output wrong. Passing tasks 47484/418-29/53161/160-6 do not hinge on ignoring a shown format → behavior unchanged. VERIFIED: the winning trials' `dd-mmm` is exactly what the new rule prescribes; the losing `d-mmm` is exactly what it forbids.

## Process & features used
- Serial (single-artifact prompt edit). Diagnosis by scripting over `./trajectories/` + the
  live `rollouts/val/` JSON: per-trial reward, final code, and — the key new signal —
  detecting the "wasted round" (tool-call-XML) error and correlating it with pass/fail
  (all 4 passing tasks = 0 wasted; failing/flaky tasks = most of the waste).
- Prior iterations read: cand_0001 PROCESS.md + JOURNAL RESULT + LEDGER. Built on its
  accepted generalization rules (kept unchanged); did NOT re-try forbidding formulas
  (cand_0001 proved 40467 passes by writing a formula — a forbid would regress it).

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- 32468 / 52216 / 347-49 / 55457 / 374-9 deep-logic errors: no safe general prompt rule
  (per-task answers; hidden test files 2&3 unavailable). The rank-1 round-1 fix gives them
  more usable rounds, which is the only safe lever prompt-only editing offers here.
- Did NOT re-add cand_0001's rejected/regressing ideas; did NOT touch a decision/permission
  rule (both edits are additive knowledge, UNBOUNDED-free by construction).
